feature: borrowed prefix slices for large ordinary gRPC unary messages

candidate.design: RequestOptions and ResponseOptions accepted a borrowed body_prefix. A gRPC unary message of at least 64 KiB wrote the five-byte frame prefix and encoded payload as separate DATA slices instead of one staged allocation.

scope.workload: ordinary gRPC unary persistent round trip, 262144-byte request and response
scope.validation: full request and response payload equality plus terminal OK

benchmark_method.schedule: five ABBA rounds; baseline, candidate, candidate, baseline
benchmark_method.host: shared host with unrelated load; no CPU pinning
benchmark_method.metric: ns_per_roundtrip from the benchmark result record

results.candidate_wins: 0/10; every candidate sample exceeded every baseline sample
results.conclusion: The candidate removed the payload-sized staging allocations, but the separate request HEADERS/DATA write path and scatter assembly cost more wall time than the removed copies.

correctness.gates_before_revert: gRPC 563/563, HTTP/2 955/955, package 26/26, grpc-cpp forward and reverse interop passed
correctness.note: correctness was not the reason for rejection; the measured wall-time regression was

resolution: Commit 0e1cef27 was reverted. The ordinary unary benchmark and build step remain as reusable evidence tooling.
